title.narrative: Stöd till UN Women Moldova för implementering av SN 2021-2022
Support to UN Women Moldova in SN 2021-2022 implementation

description.narrative: The proposed project will contribute to the full implementation of the UN Women Moldova Country Strategic Note 2018-2022. UN Women in Moldova will continue focusing on three main areas: strengthening women’s participation in politics and decision making, economic empowerment of women and ending violence against women and girls. The project will contribute to the implementation of the three Development Impact Areas: 1. Women lead, participate in and benefit equally from governance systems The Outcome under this impact area is: More women fully participate and lead in gender responsive governance processes and institutions. 2. Women have income security, decent work and economic autonomy The Outcome under this impact area is Parliament and Government adopt and implement legislation, policies and services that address unpaid domestic and care work and improve income security and decent work for women. 3. All women and girls live a life free from all forms of violence The Outcome under this impact area is: Parliament and Government adopt and implement laws, policies and strategies to prevent violence against women and girls and deliver quality essential services. Despite certain progress in strengthened legal and policy framework, improved national capacities service delivery and social mobilization for equal rights and opportunities, equality in daily life is still far from becoming a reality. UN Women will focus on working with existing challenges in the area of education, employment and political engagement, domestic violence/gender-based violence, access to justice, and in sharing, recognizing and valuing the unpaid care work.

UN Women has a long term experience in managing complex programmes in the country context and has demonstrated efficient results. Sweden has a long term positive cooperation with UN Women within several earlier and on-going contributions in Moldova. The contribution is going to address persisting gender inequalities through a comprehensive support to the three Strategic Impact Areas: Women in Leadership, Women’s Economic Empowerment and Eliminating Violence against Women and Girls. The intervention is supported by a wide group of most relevant stakeholders: the government with key ministries, the Parliament, Women's Parliamentary Caucus, local authorities, Congress of Local Authorities of Moldova, Women Mayors' Network, CSOs, women leaders and women's associations, Gender equality Platform, National Coalition of NGOs "Life Free of Violence against Women and Girls", media, academia, private sector, bilateral donors (Austria and Sweden), EU Delegation, etc. Proposed additional Swedish support for the period 2021-2022 will contribute to: • Further strengthening of the capacities of the UN Women Country Office in Moldova in the fulfilment of its core mandates: normative, operational and coordination. • Consolidation and scaling up of the UN Women’s Country Office programming capacities for the implementation of the Strategic Note for Moldova. The envisaged Swedish contribution is 30 000 000 SEK. The intervention’s total budget, including all contributors is estimated at about - 85 579 598 MSEK.

UNWOMEN har en lång erfarenhet av att hantera komplexa insatser i landet och har kunnat visa på goda resultat. Sverige har haft flera längre goda samarbeten med UNWOMEN i Moldavien. Insatsen syftar till att bekämpa rådande ojämlikheter mellan kön genom ett omfattande stöd inom tre strategiska områden: Kvinnligt ledarskap (Women in Leadership),Kvinnors ekonomiska självbestämmande (Women’s Economic Empowerment) och Bekämpandet av våld mot kvinnor och flickor (Violence against Women and Girls). Interventionen stöds av en bred grupp av de mest relevanta intressenter: regeringen med de viktigaste ministerierna, parlamentet, parlamentets kvinnogrupp, lokala myndigheter, kongressen för lokala myndigheter i Moldavien, det kvinnliga borgmästersnätverket, utomparlamentariska organisationer, kvinnliga ledare och kvinnliga föreningar, jämställdhetsplattformen, paraplyorganisationen för utomparlamentariska organisationer,”ett liv fritt från våld mot kvinnor och flickor”, media, akademin, privat sektor, bilaterala givare (Österrike och Sverige), EU-delegationen, osv. Det svenska extrastödet för perioden 2021-2022 kommer att bidra till: • Ett ytterligare stärkande av UNWOMENs landskontor i Moldavien och dess uppfyllande av dess centrala verksamhetsmandat: normativ, operativ och samordning. • Konsolidering och utökning av UNWOMENs program för genomförandet av den strategiplanen för Moldavien. Totalt uppgår det svenska anslaget till en summa av 30 000 000 SEK. Programmets totala budget, inklusive alla givares bidrag, uppskattas till 85 579 598 SEK.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
Under Women in Leadership pillar, UN Women has achieved following results:
In terms of women in leadership pillar, the effectiveness of temporary special measures in the form of gender quotas were proved in 2021, after a historical number of 40 women (39.6 per cent) were elected to Parliament due to the full application of the 40 per cent gender quota, which was strengthened in 2019 thanks to the concerted advocacy of UN Women, CSOs and development partners. This constitutes a nearly 20 per cent increase in the number of female parliamentarians in Moldova compared to 2018 (20.8 per cent), placing Moldova nearly 14 per cent ahead of the global average, which currently puts womens representation in parliaments at 26.1 per cent. The record high number of women in Parliament directly contributed to the adoption of landmark legislation, such as the ratification of the Istanbul Convention as well as normative and legal frameworks to eliminate the gender wage gap, institute alternative childcare services, combat and sanction workplace sexual harassment and abolish discriminatory provisions related to maternity leave benefits.
UN Women led participatory gender-responsive planning and budgeting processes in 20 local initiatives in partnerships with 20 women-led communities partially funded by UN Women and co-founded from Local Budgets and private citizens donations, including from diaspora.
UN Women jointly with Sweden have supported a critical and much needed law by the Womens Parliamentary Caucus - entitling mothers to receive both their full salary and maternity allowance for the period between seven months of pregnancy prior to delivery (provided they choose and are fit to work).
UN Women has helped strengthen skills, knowledge for a new generation of women from diverse groups. An Women's Advisory Board was established to advance womens meaningful participation in conflict settlement and peace processes, having civil society women leaders equally representing both banks of Nistru river.
Under Women Economic Empowerment UN Women has achieved following results:
90 women entrepreneurs expanded their businesses, through the Accelerator programme and voucher support under the area of Womens Economic Empowerment. Women business owners and small producers increased their resilience to crisis through trainings and mentorship on business and personal development, pre-accelerator/accelerator programmes as well as by accessing financial assistance through vouchers destinated for services and equipment.
A series of amendments to the Labour Code by Parliament (law #107) were developed addressing the normative framework concerning equal pay for work of equal value and responsibilities for the employers to assure equal payment for both men and women for the provided work for equal value and on reporting. 11 private sector companies increased their commitments towards gender equality and subscribed to Women Empowerment Principles in 2022.
UN Women Moldova managed to partner closely with the Economic Council to the Prime Minister and supported the development of the first ever Roadmap for Womens Economic Empowerment (WEE), as well as the creation of the specific Working Group (WG) on WEE, in which public and private sector actors, social partners and CSOs are all members.
Under the area of Ending Violence Against Women and girls, since 2018, the following results were achieved with close support of UN Women:
3 laws (laws #313, 316, 144) were approved by the Parliament aiming to allow women and girls to live free from all forms of violence. After the Istanbul Convention ratification in 2021, the new legal framework (law #316) was approved by the Parliament in November 2022. The amendments will ensure better protection for victims of gender-based violence (GBV), with a particular focus on sexual violence from a justice and law enforcement perspective.
Launching an e-learning course for social workers on addressing and referring cases of VAWG which will be compulsory as of January 2023. 61 people were registered and benefiting from the course. An optional course on Healthy Relations in the Family for students in grades eight and nine developed by a national NGO with support of UN Women, which responds to the provisions of IC on prevention of VAW, and DV.
Since the onset of the refugee crisis and beginning of the war in Ukraine, on 24 February 2022, UN Women has engaged to respond to the crisis through the coordination and operational work. On the coordination work, a Gender Task Force was established as part of the Refugee Coordination Structure under the Refugee Coordination Model, led by UN Women, and co-led by the Gender Equality Platform, having 50 partners from government bodies, UN entities, International NGOs, and local womens organizations. The program portfolio of the CO increased significantly due to refugee crisis resources mobilized and the staff increased. During the 2022 a total amount of about 9 million USD were mobilized under the SN implementation, from which 94,5% were for the humanitarian and crisis support due to the conflict and war situation in Ukraine.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
